comparator.name: Film and Literary Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 prospectus API reconstructs a complete 180-EC curriculum. The 60-EC first year and 25-EC second-year common core are compulsory. The normalized generic target does not name a specialisation; the Film Studies track is selected by the documented official-order tie break. Its 35-EC second-year track is compulsory. For the 20-EC third-year Film Studies option group, Film and Philosophy (10 EC), Third Cinema (5 EC), and Cinema & the Digital (5 EC) form a valid complete selection. The 10-EC bachelor thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space complete the degree. No optional course was selected for UCR convenience.

candidates.label: World literature, cinema and transmedial storytelling

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is generic and Leiden publishes equally general Film Studies and Literary Studies tracks after the shared first-year and common second-year core. Neither track is more representative of that shared structure. Film Studies is selected because it appears first in the current official curriculum, independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match owns the direct film-and-literature, close-reading, narrative, historical and theoretical interests. Two further generator-backed directions are coherent, feasible and materially distinct: a global and transmedial storytelling route, and a culture, identity and social-debate route. Their schedules differ pairwise by seven to fourteen courses and all satisfy the hard constraints, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

alternatives.label: Film, Literature & Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines close literary analysis with film and media studies, art history, cultural theory and humanities research, closely reflecting Leiden’s integrated text-and-image programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response combines literary interpretation with film, media and visual-cultural analysis, supported by cultural history, theory, sociology and qualitative and historical research.
progression: Introductory art history, literary studies, film and media, history and sociology precede advanced film-and-text, documentary, media, literary-theory, cultural-communication and independent-research work. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: World Literature, Cinema & Transmedial Storytelling
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum foregrounds literature and film across cultures and media, linking adaptation, media history, rhetoric, art and creative communication.
alternatives.concept: A global and transmedial route connecting world literature, cinema, adaptation, rhetoric and digital or performative communication with visual culture, philosophy and qualitative research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces Renaissance art, social theory, museum studies and historical research with rhetoric, material culture, environmental media, philosophy and advanced persuasive communication. Seven of the 24 courses differ, and its organising emphasis is global storytelling and movement across text, screen and other media.
progression: Introductions to literature, film and media, rhetoric, history and philosophy precede advanced adaptation, documentary, media-and-race, literary-theory, persuasive-communication and creative-communication work. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Culture, Identity & Social Debate
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum studies culture through history, politics, sociology, media, literature, heritage and social movements, centring identity, inequality and public debate.
alternatives.concept: A social and political cultural-analysis route organised around identity, colonialism, inequality and public debate across history, media, literature, art and heritage.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces most dedicated art-history, literary-analysis and creative-communication study with political philosophy, comparative and international politics, empire, gender history, social movements, heritage and conflict. Fourteen of the 24 courses differ, making social debate and cultural power its organising focus.
progression: Foundations in history, political philosophy, sociology, gender, ethics, comparative politics, media and literature precede advanced social theory, media and race, heritage, conflict and historical research. Every course is offered in its assigned semester; there are no unmet formal prerequisites.

blocks: Both introduce analysis of visual representation and signifying practices in historical cultural context.
Both examine representation, identity and difference across cultural and postcolonial contexts.
Both introduce literary analysis and theory through close reading and critical interpretation.
Both introduce film forms, histories and genre-based analytical concepts.
Both study literary works across historical periods and movements; UCR is comparative rather than movement-specific.
Both analyse how verbal and visual form produce meaning; UCR concentrates on rhetoric and style.
Both examine changing media technologies, histories and digital or material forms.
Both compare narrative and literary traditions across cultures and periods.
Both examine documentary form, audiovisual evidence, representation and creative non-fiction practice.
Both analyse race, representation and power in screen media; UCR is broader than the Third Cinema tradition.
Both study relations between literary texts and film, including adaptation and medium-specific meaning.
Both examine literary meaning, interpretation and non-dominant forms; UCR lacks the dedicated poetry-and-cinema pairing.
Both critically analyse contemporary audiovisual media and technology; UCR focuses on environmental media.
Both analyse films, texts and media in relation to current public and social concerns.
Both develop philosophical reasoning about value and contested judgments; UCR is not specifically philosophy of film.
Both provide philosophical foundations for questions of knowledge and method; UCR is broader than philosophy of science.
Both place cultural forms in historical movements; UCR is broad modern history rather than cinema-specific.
Both develop qualitative research, interpretation, academic writing and presentation; UCR is not limited to film and literature.
Both require sustained independent humanities research and a substantial evidence-based academic argument; UCR is a course rather than a compulsory thesis.

notes.text: Leiden requires an integrated sequence in film and literary theory, close text-image analysis, named cinematic and literary movements, world cinema and literature, adaptation and intermediality, documentary, digital cinema, a 10-EC thesis and other specialist film courses. UCR can assemble strong combinations in literature, film and media, art history, communication, philosophy, cultural history and research, but it lacks this dedicated compulsory film-and-literature sequence and has no compulsory bachelor thesis; the standardised Optional independent research element remains optional.
